idiom_name: fan-out/fan-in: N worker goroutines over one jobs channel, joined by WaitGroup
implementation_notes: Go's realization is fan-out/fan-in, as the official concurrency-patterns article describes it: one channel of jobs is read by N worker goroutines that run the identical loop and publish partial results, and closing the jobs channel is the master's end-of-work signal (a send on a closed channel panics, so exactly one owner closes it). sync.WaitGroup is the join; close(results) after Wait() lets the master range over the partials. The idiomatic unit is one goroutine per worker, not per sub-task - goroutines are cheap but a worker per task still oversubscribes the scheduler - and golang.org/x/sync/errgroup adds error propagation plus context cancellation when sub-tasks can fail. Independent goroutines must not share memory: send partials on a channel or through a slot per worker.
code_sketch:
jobs := make(chan job, len(inputs))
results := make(chan partial, len(inputs))
var wg sync.WaitGroup
for w := 0; w < workers; w++ {                       // N identical workers
    wg.Add(1)
    go func() { defer wg.Done(); for j := range jobs { results <- compute(j) } }()
}
for _, j := range inputs { jobs <- j }               // master partitions + dispatches
close(jobs)                                          // end of work
go func() { wg.Wait(); close(results) }()            // join
for p := range results { total += p.sum }            // combine
pitfalls: Goroutines are not garbage collected: a receiver that stops early leaves the senders blocked forever unless they select on a done/context channel.
Closing the jobs channel from the consumer side (or closing it twice) panics; the master must be the single closer and the workers must only receive.
An unbuffered results channel blocks a worker until the master reads, so a slow combine step throttles the whole fan-out - buffer the channel or use a dedicated collector goroutine.
Sharing a pointer to mutable state between workers by capture races; move values through channels or give each worker its own slot ('share memory by communicating').
